01 Reading ~250 words
The verb combinations from Part 1 and Part 2 are bolded in the text. Before you read the questions, try covering the story and recalling which ones you remember.
A Day Out

Sena has been looking forward to this trip for weeks — a small day out with Rio, away from their usual routine. They set off early, before the roads get busy, talking about all the places they want to visit today.

Sena has always dreamed of seeing the botanical garden they read about, with its old stone paths and imported roses. Walking through it, she stops at every flower bedcanteiro de flores · 花壇. "I could take up gardening again," she says, thinking about the small yard behind her house. "I used to care for roses when I was younger."

By noon, they're both hungry, so they look for a nice place to eat. They run into a small café near the museum, with a garden view and fresh bread. They wait for a table by the window, and Rio agrees to try the local fish, even though he usually turns down anything unfamiliar.

After lunch, they walk to the museum. Rio has always cared about photography, and he almost runs out of film for his old camera before they've even finished the first room. It takes them a while to get through the whole museum — Sena stops in front of every painting, reading each description carefully.

Not sure what to think of one of the newer exhibitspeças em exposição · 展示品, she turns to Rio for his opinion.

"I'm not sure either," he laughs. "But I'll never turn down a chance to look at something new."

On the way home, they talk about coming back next spring, when the roses will be in full bloomem plena floração · 満開. Sena dreams of painting the garden herself one day — she took up watercolorsaquarela · 水彩画 a few years ago and never quite put them down. For now, though, she puts up with the long drive home, happy and tired, already looking forward to the next trip.

02 Comprehension Questions 10 items

Answer in your own words, in full sentences. These aren't yes/no questions — explain what's happening and why.

1.What has Sena been looking forward to, and who is she spending the day with?
Sample answerShe's been looking forward to a day out with Rio, away from their usual routine.
2.What does Sena say about her own yard while they're at the botanical garden?
Sample answerShe says she could take up gardening again, thinking about the small yard behind her house — she used to care for roses when she was younger.
3.Why do they stop at a café near the museum?
Sample answerThey're hungry by noon, so they look for a place to eat and run into a small café with a garden view near the museum.
4.What does Rio agree to try at the café, and why is that unusual for him?
Sample answerHe agrees to try the local fish, which is unusual because he usually turns down anything unfamiliar.
5.What almost goes wrong for Rio at the museum?
Sample answerHe almost runs out of film for his old camera before they've even finished the first room.
6.What does Sena do while they're at the museum?
Sample answerShe takes a while to get through the whole museum, stopping in front of every painting to read the description carefully.
7.Why does Sena turn to Rio in front of one of the exhibits?
Sample answerShe's not sure what to think of one of the newer exhibits, so she turns to him for his opinion.
8.What do Sena and Rio talk about on the way home?
Sample answerThey talk about coming back next spring, when the roses will be in full bloom.
9.What hobby does Sena want to return to, according to the last paragraph?
Sample answerShe dreams of painting the garden herself — she took up watercolors a few years ago and never quite put them down.
10.How does the day end for Sena, according to the last line of the text?
Sample answerShe puts up with the long drive home, happy and tired, already looking forward to the next trip.
